saints.name: St. Margaret of Hungary
saints.title: Virgin
saints.shortBlurb: A king's daughter who was vowed to God for her country's deliverance and chose the cloister over a crown…
biography: Born at Klis in Dalmatia on 27 January 1242, while her father King Béla IV was in flight before the Mongol invasion, Margaret was vowed to God by her parents should the land be delivered. At three she was given to the Dominican nuns of Veszprém, and at ten to the convent her father founded on the Isle of Hares in the Danube near Buda, now Margaret Island.

She made her solemn vows at eighteen and, to close the door on her father's plans, received the Consecration of Virgins, refusing the hand of King Ottokar II of Bohemia. Her cloistered life was one of extreme penance, in haircloth and an iron girdle, and she chose always the meanest tasks of the house.

Worn out by austerity, she died on 18 January 1270, not yet twenty-eight. The inquest for her canonization, opened at once, recorded seventy-four miracles, yet the process failed; she was beatified in 1789 and canonized only on 19 November 1943 by Pius XII. As the king's daughter given to God for her country's deliverance, she is honored as a patron of Hungary.
saints.knownFor: Renouncing a royal marriage for the cloister.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 18 January
